definitions.explanation: A personality trait of someone who tends to worry excessively about things, even when there is no particular reason to do so. Describes a person who habitually frets and cannot relax.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{苦労性|くろうしょう}だ。
{母|はは}は{苦労性|くろうしょう}で、いつも{何|なに}かを{心配|しんぱい}している。
examples.english: My mother is a worrywart and is always worrying about something.

examples.japanese: {苦労性|くろうしょう}な{性格|せいかく}のせいで、{旅行|りょこう}の{前|まえ}はいつも{眠|ねむ}れなくなる。
examples.english: Because of my worrying nature, I always can't sleep before a trip.

notes:
Describes a temperamental tendency rather than a specific worry. The suffix {性|しょう} here indicates an innate nature or disposition (similar to {怒|おこ}りっぽい{性|しょう} but as a compound). Someone who is {苦労性|くろうしょう} worries even about things that may not warrant concern.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦労性|くろうしょう}な{人|ひと}: a person with a worrying disposition
- {苦労性|くろうしょう}な{性格|せいかく}: a worrying personality

RELATED WORDS:
- {心配性|しんぱいしょう}: worrywart — very similar, slightly more common
- {苦労知|くろうし}らず: carefree, having no hardships — the opposite type
- {気苦労|きぐろう}: mental stress, worry — the stress itself
- {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|ぐろう}: needless worry, borrowing trouble
